import { existsSync, readFileSync, writeFileSync, mkdirSync, statSync } from 'node:fs'
import { resolve, join, extname } from 'node:path'
import { createHash } from 'node:crypto'
import { createServer } from 'node:http'
import { spawn } from 'node:child_process'
import { pathToFileURL } from 'node:url'
import { child } from './session-lifecycle.mjs'
import { livePreviewScript, watchProject } from './live-preview.mjs'

export function projectType(root) {
  if (existsSync(join(root, 'package.json'))) {
    const p = JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(root, 'package.json'), 'utf8'))
    if (p.dependencies?.next || p.devDependencies?.next) throw new Error('Unsupported framework: customize start.sh and provide static deployment output.')
    if (p.dependencies?.vite || p.devDependencies?.vite) return 'vite'
    throw new Error('Unsupported package project: customize start.sh and deployment output.')
  }
  if (existsSync(join(root, 'index.html'))) return 'html'
  throw new Error('No generated index.html or supported package project.')
}
export async function start(root = process.cwd()) {
  const type = projectType(root)
  const projectRoot = resolve(root)
  if (type === 'vite') {
    const stampDir = process.env.OPENCODE_WEB_DIR || join(root, 'node_modules', '.cache')
    mkdirSync(stampDir, { recursive: true })
    const stamp = join(stampDir, 'default-dependencies')
    const lock = join(root, 'package-lock.json')
    const hash = createHash('sha256').update(readFileSync(join(root, 'package.json'))).update(existsSync(lock) ? readFileSync(lock) : '').digest('hex')
    let old = ''
    try { old = readFileSync(stamp, 'utf8') } catch {}
    if (old !== hash || !existsSync(join(root, 'node_modules/vite'))) {
      await child('npm', [existsSync(lock) ? 'ci' : 'install', '--no-audit', '--no-fund'], { cwd: root })
      mkdirSync(stampDir, { recursive: true })
      const installedHash = createHash('sha256').update(readFileSync(join(root, 'package.json'))).update(existsSync(lock) ? readFileSync(lock) : '').digest('hex')
      writeFileSync(stamp, installedHash)
    }
    await child(process.execPath, [join(root, 'node_modules/vite/bin/vite.js'), 'build', '--base', './'], { cwd: root })
    root = join(root, 'dist')
  }
  if (!existsSync(join(root, 'index.html'))) throw new Error('Static deployment output must contain index.html.')
  if (process.env.OPENCODE_WEB_DIR) writeFileSync(join(process.env.OPENCODE_WEB_DIR, 'deployment-output.json'), JSON.stringify({ project: projectRoot, directory: resolve(root) }))
  const mime = { '.html':'text/html', '.js':'application/javascript', '.css':'text/css', '.json':'application/json', '.svg':'image/svg+xml', '.png':'image/png', '.jpg':'image/jpeg', '.webp':'image/webp', '.wasm':'application/wasm', '.glb':'model/gltf-binary' }
  const clients = new Set()
  const stopWatching = watchProject(root, () => { for (const client of clients) client.write('event: change\ndata: changed\n\n') })
  const keepAlive = setInterval(() => { for (const client of clients) client.write(': keepalive\n\n') }, 20000)
  const buildWatcher = type === 'vite' ? spawn(process.execPath, [join(projectRoot, 'node_modules/vite/bin/vite.js'), 'build', '--base', './', '--watch'], { cwd: projectRoot, stdio: 'inherit' }) : null
  const server = createServer((req, res) => {
    try {
      const url = new URL(req.url, 'http://localhost')
      if (url.pathname === '/__omgithub/live') {
        res.writeHead(200, { 'Content-Type': 'text/event-stream', 'Cache-Control': 'no-cache', 'X-Accel-Buffering': 'no', Connection: 'keep-alive' })
        res.write(': connected\n\n')
        clients.add(res)
        req.on('close', () => clients.delete(res))
        return
      }
      const path = resolve(root, '.' + decodeURIComponent(url.pathname))
      if (path !== resolve(root) && !path.startsWith(resolve(root) + '/')) { res.writeHead(404); res.end(); return }
      const file = statSync(path).isDirectory() ? join(path, 'index.html') : path
      res.setHeader('Content-Type', mime[extname(file)] || 'application/octet-stream')
      res.setHeader('Cache-Control', url.searchParams.has('omgithub_live') ? 'no-store' : 'no-cache')
      const content = readFileSync(file)
      if (extname(file) === '.html' && url.searchParams.get('omgithub_live') === '1') {
        const html = content.toString()
        res.end(/<\/body\s*>/i.test(html) ? html.replace(/<\/body\s*>/i, `${livePreviewScript}</body>`) : html + livePreviewScript)
      } else res.end(content)
    } catch { res.writeHead(404); res.end('Not found') }
  })
  server.on('close', () => { stopWatching(); clearInterval(keepAlive); buildWatcher?.kill(); for (const client of clients) client.end() })
  server.listen(Number(process.env.PORT || 3000), '0.0.0.0')
  return server
}
if (process.argv[1] && import.meta.url === pathToFileURL(process.argv[1]).href) await start()
import { startForCapture } from './capture-start.mjs'
import captures from './wip-screenshots.cjs'
import { createRequire } from 'node:module'
import { readFileSync, mkdirSync } from 'node:fs'
import { join } from 'node:path'
const runtime = join(process.env.HOME, '.local/share/omgithub-playwright')
const require = createRequire(join(runtime, 'package.json'))
const { chromium } = require('playwright')
captures.instrument({ chromium })
const config = JSON.parse(readFileSync(join(runtime, process.platform === 'darwin' ? 'metal.json' : 'linux.json'), 'utf8'))
if (process.platform === 'linux') process.env.DISPLAY ||= ':' + readFileSync(join(runtime, 'display'), 'utf8').trim()
const url = process.env.CAPTURE_URL, output = process.env.CAPTURE_DIR
if (!url || !output) throw new Error('Set CAPTURE_URL and CAPTURE_DIR.')
mkdirSync(output, { recursive: true })
const transient = error => { throw Object.assign(error, { exitCode: 75 }) }
let browser
try {
  browser = await chromium.launch({ ...config.browser.launchOptions, timeout: 30000 }).catch(transient)
  for (const [name, width, height] of [['desktop', 1440, 900], ['mobile', 390, 844]]) {
    const page = await browser.newPage({ viewport: { width, height } }).catch(transient)
    page.setDefaultTimeout(30000)
    const failures = []
    page.on('pageerror', error => { console.error(error.message); failures.push(error.message) })
    page.on('response', response => { if (response.status() >= 400 && new URL(response.url()).origin === new URL(url).origin) failures.push(`HTTP ${response.status()}: ${response.url()}`) })
    const response = await page.goto(url, { waitUntil: 'load', timeout: 45000 }).catch(transient)
    if (!response?.ok()) throw Object.assign(new Error(`HTTP ${response?.status()} loading preview`), { exitCode: !response || [408, 429, 500, 502, 503, 504].includes(response.status()) ? 75 : 1 })
    await page.locator(process.env.CAPTURE_READY_SELECTOR || 'body').waitFor({ state: 'visible' })
    await page.waitForFunction(() => document.fonts.status === 'loaded')
    const start = await startForCapture(page, {
      enabled: process.env.CAPTURE_AUTO_START !== 'false',
      selector: process.env.CAPTURE_START_SELECTOR || ''
    })
    console.log(`Capture ${name}: auto-start ${start.clicked ? 'clicked' : start.reason}`)
    await page.waitForTimeout(1000)
    await page.screenshot({ path: join(output, `final-${name}.png`), timeout: 30000 }).catch(error => {
      if (error.name === 'TimeoutError' || !browser.isConnected()) transient(error)
      throw error
    })
    if (process.env.CAPTURE_STRICT === '1' && failures.length) throw new Error(`Published build failed: ${failures.join('; ')}`)
    await page.close()
  }
} catch (error) { console.error(error); process.exitCode = error.exitCode || 1 }
finally { await browser?.close().catch(error => { console.error(error); process.exitCode ||= 75 }) }

Plan:
- Static site: index.html, styles.css, src/main.js, maybe vendor/three.module.js.

- Game: skate park with ramps, rails, ledges, quarter pipes. Player skater model built from primitives with animated pose, board with wheels. Physics custom: velocity, steering, friction, gravity on ramps, ollie, manuals? "like Skate" — flick controls: use right stick flicks for tricks. On touch: swipe gestures on right side to trick (ollie, kickflip, heelflip, shuvit, 360 flip, grind). Left virtual joystick for movement. On gamepad: left stick move, right stick flick tricks, buttons jump/grind, triggers accelerate.

Implement trick detection: right stick flick directions. For touch, drag on trick pad. Skate-like controls: down-right flick etc. Simpler: directional flicks + combos:
- Swipe up = Ollie
- Swipe down = Manual? Maybe crouch/charge
- Swipe left = Kickflip, right = Heelflip, up-right = 360 flip, etc.
Also dedicated buttons for easy play: Kickflip, Heelflip, Shuvit, Grind, Ollie. Hmm, touch controls need to be usable. Do both: big buttons on right for Ollie/Trick and left stick for steering; plus swipe pad.

Grinds: when near rail and holding grind button / jump onto it, lock onto rail, score multiplier, balance meter with left-right.

Score, combo, timer? Skate games: session with score and challenges. Add "S-K-A-T-E" challenge? Could do 2-minute run with score, combo multiplier, and best score localStorage. Add collectible S-K-A-T-E letters maybe. Keep scope.

Now design game. Need high quality visually and gameplay. Let's think deeply about implementation.

Tech: Three.js r166 module. Static HTML served by default static server. Use importmap or direct relative import. Since vendor/three.module.js is module, use `<script type="module" src="./src/main.js">` and `import * as THREE from '../vendor/three.module.js'`.

Rendering: WebGLRenderer antialias, shadows PCFSoft, ACES tone mapping, fog, sky gradient via shader or large sphere with vertex colors. Scene is a skate park with:
- ground concrete plaza (large box/plane)
- quarter pipes (curved ramps generated with ExtrudeGeometry? easier Lathe? Custom geometry using parametric surface).
- funbox with ramps
- rails (metal cylinders + posts)
- ledges
- halfpipe maybe.
- obstacles for grinds: rails and ledges tagged with grind paths (line segments), plus manual pads.
- ramps: incline surfaces for physics via height function. Simpler: define ramp collision as oriented boxes with surface height? For skate feel, need transitions.

Physics approach: 2.5D-ish 3D on a heightfield defined analytically. Player position (x,z), y from ground height plus vertical velocity. Ground height function composed of:
- flat plaza y=0
- ramps: quarter pipes have curved transition. Compute height as a function of distance into ramp, with lip. Could represent ramps as boxes that raise the ground height for x/z inside; but riding up vertical wall weird. Use smooth functions.

Alternative: Use simple "grind/ramp zones": ramps are physically modeled by height function where approach from one direction yields curved slope. For quarter pipes positioned at edges, easier create halfpipe ramps along x direction with height as function of z near edges. Player moves around; transitions raise up.

Let's design a plaza 70x50:
- Main flat area.
- North edge z=-18: quarter pipe spanning x from -20 to 20, rises toward -z? If player near north edge, height increases smoothly. Add lip. But "height function" groundHeight(x,z) used for both visuals? Visual ramp custom geometry built to match function.

Could use heightmap grid sampled from analytic height function for all ramps and render a deformed PlaneGeometry (vertex heights). Then physics uses same heightAt(x,z) bilinear interpolation. Nice! Build a 100x100 subdivided plane 80x60, with height function combining ramp features and bowl. Render concrete material with subtle texture generated via canvas. Great.

Define height function:
- base 0.
- Quarter pipe along north edge: for z < -14, h = R * (1 - sqrt(1 - t^2))? Actually transition: h = r - sqrt(r^2 - d^2) where d is distance from ramp start, capped at lip angle. For approach from z > -14, d = (-14 - z), for d in [0, 8.4], radius r=8.4 gives vertical at d=8.4. Height goes 0 to 8.4. But mesh can have vertical face. Physics: when riding up transition, gravity along slope slows player; if reaches lip with speed, launch into air (need detect leaving ground).

Interesting: hiding scene children progressively increased fps from 4 to 24 as more hidden; but it's cumulative by 10, and fps jumps around hidden 100+ to 24. The biggest fps jumps:
- hidden 0-9 → 5.3 (sky/sun/clouds)
- 10-19 → 10
- 20-29 → 12
- 60-69 → 12
- 70-79 → 14.7
- 80-89 → 18
- 90-99 → 19.3
- 100-109 → 23.3
- 110-119 → 24.7
then plateaus 24 even as more hidden. So many draw calls each cost. By hiding ~120 children fps reaches 24; hiding rest doesn't improve further due likely baseline or not all hidden (rendering scene with 300 children). The progression means object count/draw calls is the bottleneck, not fill rate. 300 top-level children; many meshes. 24fps when hiding first 120 objects, which correspond to buildings/city/rail etc. Hmm.

Wait 300 top-level children! Scene children includes every building (46), ground decals, each rail group, palms etc. Hiding by scene children index 100+ didn't further improve after 24; maybe the remaining are groups whose children still render? No, hiding group hides children. But after hiding 120 children, remaining ~180 might be mostly hidden by frustum? The baseline 24 suggests 24fps cap by something else, maybe rAF in headed Xvfb at 24? Blank was 54. Maybe the render loop includes expensive JS/physics? The scene has ~200 meshes in frustum. Hmm.

Actually in the perfscene loop, hiding groups by index, but setting `visible=false` on scene children does hide them. At hidden 110-119, 120 objects hidden, still 180 visible. FPS 24. Then hiding further 180 objects doesn't increase → perhaps the remaining visible objects are outside camera frustum and renderer culls them, so rendering only ~? and we hit some bottleneck such as three.js matrix updates for 300 objects? Still no.

Could be that after page starts, timer animation and skater; but 24fps cap might be Xvfb/screen. Blank 54.

Anyway, reducing draw calls drastically (palms, buildings) should improve significantly. The biggest object count categories:
- buildings 46 (scene children indices 15-60)
- palms 17*6 = 102 (indices 68-87 groups? Actually 82-87 each 17 = 102)
- rails 4*~13 = 52
- walls groups etc.
Hiding 0-119 covered buildings + palms + some rails/walls and fps reached 24. Yes! So buildings+palms+rails are the cost. Great. Let's instance palms and city, and merge rail geometries where possible.

For rails, each has top + posts + feet + bands ~13 meshes. 4 rails→52. Could merge per rail into one BufferGeometry manually (all cylinders and boxes can be merged by creating geometries transformed and using BufferGeometryUtils; we can implement a small merge function). Or simpler: use InstancedMesh for rails? Each piece differs; but we can create one `InstancedMesh` of cylinders for all posts across rails, one for feet, one for top tubes? Top tubes differ in length; can use instance scaling along Y then rotate. Cylinder geometry unit height 1, scale y=length. Great: 
- posts: one InstancedMesh cylinder unit (radius .05, height 1) with matrices (scale y=height) for all posts; feet: cylinder; tops: cylinder unit height 1 scaled; bands: cylinder scaled .26. 4 draw calls total.
- But colors/materials differ? Use same metal/darkMetal. Could make tops metal, posts dark metal: 2 instanced meshes for posts, feet + 1 top + bands (orange material). 3-4 draw calls vs 52.
- Need handles for top tube positions; can compute matrices.

However current buildRail adds group per rail. We can refactor to accumulate matrices in arrays and create instanced meshes at end. Or easier, use a local `collectRailParts` returning arrays and buildInstanced at end of createWorld. This is a bit of code.

Palms: Build InstancedMesh for trunk segments (cylinder geometry) all palms, and leaves (ShapeGeometry) all palms. Need per-instance matrix with scale/rotation. 2 draw calls vs 102. Great.
